Trail Physics · Unit 1: Physics Foundations · Module 1

Introduction to Physics

What physics studies, how scientists build models and laws, and why a mountain bike is a physical system.

Lesson in review

The question

What’s actually happening, physically, when you ride a bike down a trail?

The physics

  • What physics studies
  • Scientific models
  • Laws and theories
  • Physical systems
  • Observation and evidence

Learning objectives

  • Describe what physics studies, with examples from riding
  • Identify the physical phenomena happening during a ride
  • Tell matter, energy, motion and interactions apart in a riding situation
  • Tell an observation, a model, a law and a theory apart
  • Describe a mountain bike as a physical system of interacting parts
  • Name the physics each part of a bike depends on
  • Tell observations, explanations and predictions apart
  • Plan an investigation and name its independent, dependent and controlled variables
  • Name the main branches of physics and connect each to riding

The mountain biking connection

A mountain bike is a system of interacting parts: wheels that rotate, tires that grip, springs that compress, brakes that turn motion into heat. Each part is a way into physics.

Learning activities

Interactive lesson

Introduction to Physics

Find the physics hiding on the trail, ride one run through seven physics lessons, then learn how physicists choose systems, build models and design experiments, and become a physics detective.

Level

Time

  • Find the Physics
  • One ride, seven lessons
  • Experiment designer
